summary.short: SIC Circular Externa 005 of 2017 adds Chapter Three to Title V of the Circular Única on international transfers of personal data. It sets the standards for an adequate level of protection in recipient countries, lists countries considered adequate, and sets a declaration-of-conformity procedure for other transfers.
summary.long: Colombia's Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) issued Circular Externa 005 of 10 August 2017, adding Chapter Three to Title V of the Circular Única. It applies to controllers (Responsables) and processors (Encargados) that transfer personal data to other countries, and it builds on Article 26 of Statutory Law 1581 of 2012, which prohibits transfers to countries without an adequate level of protection, subject to listed exceptions (express authorisation, medical data, banking transfers, treaties, contract performance, public interest or judicial claims). The Circular sets six standards for adequate protection (rules, principles, data subject rights, duties, judicial and administrative remedies, and a supervisory authority). It gives a non-exhaustive list of countries the SIC considers adequate, which the SIC may revise at any time. Controllers must still demonstrate accountability measures when transferring to listed countries. For other transfers, controllers may request a declaration of conformity under the procedure in Section 3.3. A contract or other instrument guaranteeing compliance creates a presumption of viability, with prior communication to the SIC. Mere transit of data through other territories is not a transfer. Breaches may be investigated and sanctioned. The Circular takes effect on publication in the Diario Oficial.

evidence.quote: El tránsito transfronterizo de datos se refiere al simple paso de los datos por uno o varios territorios utilizando la infraestructura compuesta por todas las redes, equipos y servicios requeridos para alcanzar su destino final.

El análisis para establecer si un país ofrece un nivel adecuado de protección de datos personales, a efectos de realizar una transferencia internacional de datos, estará orientado a determinar si dicho país garantiza la protección de los mismos, con base en los siguientes estándares:

obligations.summary: The SIC's analysis of whether a receiving country offers an adequate level of protection must be oriented to whether that country guarantees protection, based on standards (a) to (f) listed in section 3.1.
obligations.applies_from: from publication in the Diario Oficial (Sec. 4)

evidence.quote: estará orientado a determinar si dicho país garantiza la protección de los mismos, con base en los siguientes estándares

obligations.summary: The SIC exercises its regulatory capacity at any time to review the list of countries with an adequate level of protection and to add or exclude countries.
obligations.applies_from: from publication in the Diario Oficial (Sec. 4)

evidence.quote: La Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio ejercerá, en cualquier tiempo, su capacidad regulatoria para revisar la lista anterior

obligations.summary: Even when transferring to a country with an adequate level of protection, controllers must be able to demonstrate appropriate and effective measures to ensure proper processing of the transferred data and security of the records at the time of transfer.
obligations.applies_from: from publication in the Diario Oficial (Sec. 4)
obligations.conditional_on: transfer to a country on the adequate-protection list in num. 3.2

evidence.quote: los Responsables del Tratamiento, en virtud del principio de responsabilidad demostrada, deben ser capaces de demostrar que han implementado medidas apropiadas y efectivas

obligations.summary: For a transfer to a country not on the list, the controller making the transfer must verify whether the operation falls within an exception in Article 26 of Law 1581 of 2012, or whether the country meets the standards in num. 3.1; if neither applies, it must request a declaration of conformity from the SIC.
obligations.applies_from: from publication in the Diario Oficial (Sec. 4)
obligations.conditional_on: transfer to a country not on the list in num. 3.2

evidence.quote: corresponderá al Responsable del tratamiento que efectuará la transferencia verificar si la operación está comprendida dentro de una de las causales de excepción

obligations.summary: To request a declaration of conformity, the controller must file a petition with the SIC, providing the information in the SIC's published guide; supporting documents sent must be translated into Spanish.
obligations.applies_from: from publication in the Diario Oficial (Sec. 4)
obligations.conditional_on: request for a declaration of conformity

evidence.quote: el Responsable del tratamiento deberá radicar una petición ante la Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio

obligations.summary: Where the controller signs a transfer contract or other legal instrument setting conditions and guarantees, the transfer may proceed after prior communication to the SIC's Delegatura para la Protección de Datos Personales describing the operation and declaring that the contract or instrument has been signed; the operation is then presumed viable.
obligations.applies_from: from publication in the Diario Oficial (Sec. 4)
obligations.conditional_on: controller has signed a transfer contract or other legal instrument ensuring protection

evidence.quote: previa comunicación remitida a la Delegatura para la Protección de Datos Personales de la Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio

enforcement.triggered_by: Evidenced non-compliance with the conditions of a transfer for which the controller has signed a transfer contract or other instrument and notified the Delegatura, as verified by the SIC at any time
enforcement.max_penalty_text: No amount or sanction type is stated in this text; it refers only to 'las sanciones que correspondan'

evidence.quote: en caso de que se evidencie un incumplimiento, podrá adelantar la respectiva investigación e imponer las sanciones que correspondan y ordenar las medidas a que haya lugar

thresholds.note: The circular sets qualitative adequacy standards (items a) to f) of num. 3.1) and a list of countries (num. 3.2). It contains no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. The 'tres supuestos' in Sec. 2 is a count of legal routes, not a threshold.
